goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — LoggerMiddleware no longer adds pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID and relies on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain; any chain without it (or reordered) silently drops these fields, and no test covers either middleware's log output.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows LoggerMiddleware no longer appends request identity fields itself: logRequest dropped pluginCtx/endpoint parameters and removed adding pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID, and now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go). Those attributes are instead added only by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext()` using `log.WithContextualAttributes(...)` (contextual_logger_middleware.go), and CreateMiddlewares wires it before LoggerMiddleware (pluginsintegration.go). This creates an ordering/usage coupling: any middleware stack that omits or reorders ContextualLoggerMiddleware would lose those fields without an explicit guard. The diff also doesn’t add any tests asserting the structured log output for either middleware.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go:59 — Stream endpoints (SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream) pass through without contextual attributes, so logs further down the chain for streaming requests have no pluginId/endpoint/user context.

adjudication.rationale: In `contextual_logger_middleware.go`, `instrumentContext(...)` is applied only in `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics`, but `SubscribeStream`, `PublishStream`, and `RunStream` simply call `m.next.*` without wrapping the context. Given this middleware’s stated purpose (“adds a contextual logger to the request context”), streaming RPCs won’t get the added attributes (`endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName/dsUID`, `uname`) from this middleware, so downstream logging that relies on context enrichment will miss them for streaming endpoints. This is an incomplete coverage concern rather than a clear functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:49 — Exported NewLoggerMiddleware now silently depends on NewContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain; any other chain composing it alone drops pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID from the grafana-data-egress "Plugin Request Completed" log line.

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go, logRequest no longer appends plugin/request fields (pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID, traceID) to logParams and instead logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is what adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` into the context via `log.WithContextualAttributes` (contextual_logger_middleware.go). CreateMiddlewares now orders `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)`, so the default stack keeps those fields, but `NewLoggerMiddleware` used without that preceding middleware will indeed drop them. This is a real, diff-grounded coupling/ordering concern, though not necessarily a runtime defect in the shown integration path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go:79 — NewMetricsMiddleware mutates a single shared MetricsMiddleware's next field each time the middleware func is applied, so decorating more than one client makes every decorated client route to the last-wrapped next (carried over from the old instrumentation middleware).

adjudication.rationale: In `NewMetricsMiddleware`, a single `*MetricsMiddleware` instance (`imw := newMetricsMiddleware(...)`) is created and then reused for every application of the returned `ClientMiddlewareFunc`. The closure mutates `imw.next = next` and returns the same `imw` pointer each time. If the same middleware value is applied to decorate more than one client, the `next` field will be overwritten and all previously decorated clients will end up calling the most recently assigned `next`, matching the finding’s described routing bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:49 — FromContext type-asserts the infra log interface to *log.ConcreteLogger and silently falls back to d.New(), dropping all contextual attributes if the concrete type ever changes (leaky type boundary).

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, the new grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) and then type-asserts the result to *log.ConcreteLogger. If that assertion fails, it silently returns d.New() (with no ctx), which would not carry any contextual attributes derived from the provided context. This creates a leaky boundary on the concrete logger type and a potentially lossy fallback behavior, even if it may not fail with today’s infra logger implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:46 — TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger, so logs emitted via FromContext (as LoggerMiddleware now does) are never recorded on the fake and cannot be asserted in tests.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go the new method `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` returns a brand-new logger instance rather than a contextualized view of the same `TestLogger`. Since `LoggerMiddleware` was changed to emit logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, any code/tests using `TestLogger` will record the log call on the new instance, not on the original fake (`f`), making emitted logs invisible to assertions on the original fake.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:58 — LoggerMiddleware now implicitly depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain to get pluginId/endpoint/uname/ds fields; this hidden ordering coupling is undocumented and silently degrades logs if the order changes.

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go, LoggerMiddleware.logRequest no longer receives pluginCtx/endpoint and no longer appends pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID (and traceID) to logParams; instead it logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, relying on those attributes having been injected into `ctx` elsewhere. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is what adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` via `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` (contextual_logger_middleware.go). CreateMiddlewares currently orders ContextualLoggerMiddleware before LoggerMiddleware, but this dependency is implicit: if middleware order changes or LoggerMiddleware is used without ContextualLoggerMiddleware, logs will silently lose those fields. This is a real ordering/architecture coupling introduced by the diff, but not a direct functional defect given the current order in the diff.
